status: prototype - not a final production spec, see docs/animation-policy.md

pivot.basis: fixed across all animations/frames of this character; horizontal = shared silhouette center, vertical = lowest observed hover-pod position among the adopted Idle frames (virtual ground line). proto_one is a hover-type character with no literal foot contact. Walking and Sprinting both reuse this exact pivot (not independently re-fit) so switching between animations in-game does not pop the character's position or scale. EXCEPTION: SlowFalling's body-bottom lands at output row 106.3, not 123 (updated again 2026-09-11: after two attempts still clipped the flame, the priority was flipped to guarantee zero clipping of both the antenna tip and flame tip, at the cost of a larger pivot deviation and a slightly smaller character than Idle's reference size). See SlowFalling's own notes for the full history and numbers.

Turn.notes: One-shot direction-change transition, not a looping locomotion cycle: frame 00 = facing left, frame 01 = stylized spin/twist motion-blur effect, frame 02 = facing right. No corresponding code MovementState exists yet (see animation-policy.md); this is asset-only preparation ahead of movement-logic wiring.

Jumping.notes: One-shot takeoff sequence (matches code MovementState Jumping, which the doc's animation vocabulary calls Jump Start + Airborne combined), not a repeating cycle - frame 00 = ready/crouch pose, frame 01 = thrust launch with visible downward propulsion trail from all 3 hover pods, frame 02 = airborne pose. fps/loop are independent candidates, not part of the Current Animation Contract.

Falling.notes: Unlike Turn/Jumping, Falling loops: descent duration is variable (depends on fall height/state), not a fixed one-shot burst, so it is treated as a sustained state like Idle/Walking/Sprinting rather than a bounded transition. fps=6 is an unconfirmed independent candidate, not part of the Current Animation Contract.

FastFalling.notes: SUPERSEDES an earlier decision recorded in the top-level notes to keep fast_falling01+02: the user clarified FastFalling is meant to be a distinct 'more extreme dive' feel, and that 01/02 read as too weak in actual gameplay - 03/04 were generated specifically as stronger-smear replacements for 01/02, not as an extension of them. Source swapped 2026-09-11 (later same day) to fast_falling03.png + fast_falling04.png; fast_falling01.png and 02.png remain on disk but are no longer used by this animation. Like Falling, FastFalling is a sustained state of variable duration (held until the dive input/state ends), not a one-shot burst, so loop=true. fps=10 (vs Falling's 6) is an unconfirmed independent candidate chosen to read faster/more urgent.

AirDashing.notes: One-shot burst matching the ~0.14s air dash duration from the movement prototype (project-brief.md), re-triggered fresh on each new dash rather than held/looped - 3 frames at 20fps play out in 0.15s, close to that duration. All 3 raw frames use the same dash-stretch + cyan afterimage/speed-particle visual language per animation-policy.md section 8. Body-silhouette measurement (glow/streak pixels excluded via the blue-channel filter, verified against a debug mask) found frame 1 (air_dashing_02) a uniform-scale outlier - 102x91px on the 128 canvas vs 109x97 and 103x103 for the other two - so it alone was corrected via pivot-anchored rescale (x1.069 about the fixed pivot (64,123)), landing at 110x98px, in range with the others. fps/loop are independent candidates, not part of the Current Animation Contract.

SlowFalling.notes: SUPERSEDES two earlier SlowFalling attempts (backed up at proto_one.manifest.json.bak-before-slowfalling and .bak-before-slowfalling-v2). Attempt 1 (original raw art): fixed scale to match Idle's body height exactly, accepted a 10px pivot deviation, flame clipped to ~38-40% visible. Attempt 2 (raw art regenerated with a shorter flame): same method, pivot deviation improved to 5.5px, flame visibility improved to ~59% - but the user pointed out frame 2's flame was STILL visibly clipped. Root cause found on inspection: this method was choosing cropY0 to maximize pivot accuracy first and only checking a flame-length FLOOR, not verifying the full flame tip actually fit inside the crop - and separately, the 'body-only' bbox measurement (which the scale was matched against) excludes the antenna's thin pointed tip because it's too narrow to pass the row-width threshold used to separate body from glow, so it was never being protected from clipping either. ATTEMPT 3 (this one, same raw frames as attempt 2): changed the method's priority order entirely - zero clipping of BOTH the antenna tip and the flame tip is now the primary hard constraint, with a small explicit safety margin (5 output px on each end), and character size is whatever falls out of that (no longer force-matched to Idle's exact height). Concretely: measured the TRUE full-alpha extent (threshold>=200, no glow exclusion, so antenna tip and flame tip are both included) across both frames - top=67 (antenna tip, both frames identical), bottom=1176 (frame 2's flame tip, the longer of the two) - content span 1110px. Solved for the crop side that fits this span plus 5px of margin on each side once scaled to 128: side=1205, scale=0.1062. This is smaller (character renders smaller) than the Idle-matched scale used in attempts 1-2 (0.1340 / 0.1150) - resulting body size is ~90px by the same body-only measurement, about 7.7% smaller than Idle's 97.5px reference, and pivot deviation grew to 16.7px (body-bottom lands at output row 106.3, not 123) - both explicitly accepted as the cost of guaranteeing zero clipping, which is what the user actually asked for after seeing attempt 2. Contact sheet confirms both frames now show the complete flame (including frame 2's longer one) and complete antenna with real margin on both ends, nothing touching the canvas edge. Both frames still share one identical crop rectangle (cropX0=49, cropY0=20, side=1205), so body size and position remain pixel-identical between the two frames. fps=7, loop=true unchanged.

Landing.notes: Land=4 was adopted in animation-policy.md's Current Animation Contract as a NEW row (Land did not previously exist in the contract table, only as a non-binding candidate of ~1) - raw source had exactly 4 frames, far exceeding that candidate, so before adopting all 4 each was measured (full-alpha bbox threshold>=200, plus body-silhouette bbox with the usual blue-channel glow exclusion) to rule out a Turn-style mixed-category set or an FastFalling-style redundant/weak subset. Result: body aspect ratio (H/W) moves 0.764 (landing_01) -> 0.636 (landing_02, most squashed - widest and shortest) -> 1.001 (landing_03) -> 0.967 (landing_04, settled near-round), a genuine single-direction impact-compress-then-recover trajectory, not a mix of pose categories or a redundant near-duplicate pair - so all 4 were adopted rather than curating a subset. This matches animation-policy.md section 7's description of Land as 'a brief impact compression', just spread across 4 frames instead of implied as roughly 1. Normalized using the standard method (same as Jumping/Falling/AirDashing): shared crop fit to the union of all 4 frames' full alpha bbox (threshold>=200, no glow exclusion) with a 6px safety margin on top and both sides, positioned so the fixed pivot (64,123) sits at the union's max-Y (lowest point across all frames) - side=990, scale=0.1293, cropX0=132, cropY0=106, identical for all 4 frames. No per-frame outlier rescale was applied: the aspect-ratio swing across frames is the intentional squash-and-stretch of the impact itself (confirmed by the smooth, monotonic-looking progression above), not uniform-scale jitter like Walking/Falling's corrected outliers - closer in nature to Jumping's uncorrected pod-tuck pose difference. Contact sheet confirms no clipping on any frame, with visible margin on antenna, wheels, and glow on all 4. Land has no corresponding code MovementState yet (see animation-policy.md's 'code에 대응이 없는 문서 상태' list, same situation as Turn) - this is asset-only preparation ahead of movement-logic wiring, per animation-policy.md item 6 in the implementation-order list. loop=false since this is a one-shot impact-then-settle transition, not a held/looping state, matching Turn/Jumping/AirDashing rather than Idle/Walking/Falling. fps=16 is an unconfirmed independent candidate chosen for a snappy, sub-0.3s impact read; not part of the Current Animation Contract, which governs frame count only.

WallSliding.notes: WallSliding=4 was adopted in animation-policy.md's Current Animation Contract, upgrading the row from TBD (raw source had exactly 4 frames, exceeding the non-binding Wall/Hang candidate range of ~1-3 - documented as such per the usual 'candidate table is advisory, not binding' rule). Raw frames render with an opaque-looking solid black background in casual preview, unlike every prior state's raw art which previewed with a transparent/white background - this was flagged and verified directly at the pixel level before trusting it (same discipline as the FastFalling checkerboard investigation): sampled corner pixels are RGBA(0,0,0,0) (true alpha=0) on all 4 frames, and a sampled alpha histogram across each full frame shows a clean binary split (alpha=0 background / alpha=255 character, no edge-noise cluster in between) - the solid-black look is a preview-rendering quirk only, not a real transparency defect, so no sanitization was needed before normalizing. Before adopting all 4 frames, measured full-alpha bbox (threshold>=200) per frame: X range is pixel-identical across all 4 (X[234,1059]) and Y range varies by only 11px (196-212 top, 1055-1057 bottom) - character position and pose are effectively pinned, with only the left-side thruster/exhaust effect's length and shape flickering frame to frame. This is unlike Landing's genuine multi-frame pose progression or Turn's mixed pose+effect categories - it reads as a held idle-style loop with a flickering effect, so all 4 were kept as a loop rather than curated down. Normalized using the standard method (same as Jumping/Falling/AirDashing/Landing): shared crop fit to the union of all 4 frames' full alpha bbox with a 6px safety margin on top and both sides, positioned so the fixed pivot (64,123) sits at the union's max-Y - side=944, scale=0.1356, cropX0=174, cropY0=150, identical for all 4 frames. No per-frame outlier rescale was needed given how tightly the bboxes already agree. Contact sheet confirms no clipping and consistent pivot alignment across all 4 frames. Unlike Turn and Land, WallSliding already exists as a value in the code's `MovementState` enum (src/Player.hpp) - a genuine held movement state, not an asset-only overlay - so loop=true was chosen (character stays in this state for a variable duration while in wall contact, like Falling/SlowFalling/FastFalling rather than Turn/Jumping/AirDashing/Landing's one-shot bursts). fps=6 is an unconfirmed independent candidate chosen for a slow, held flicker read; not part of the Current Animation Contract, which governs frame count only.

Turn=3 frames was adopted in animation-policy.md's Current Animation Contract as a NEW row (Turn did not previously exist in the contract table) - the raw source had exactly 3 frames, which exceeds the old non-binding candidate range of ~1-2 but the candidate table is explicitly advisory, not binding, so the actual provided asset count was adopted. Turn's 3 raw frames are not simply pose variations of one category: frame 1 and frame 3 are mirrored static facing poses (left vs right), while frame 2 is a categorically different stylized spin/twist motion-blur effect frame. The body-silhouette-outlier check was applied ONLY between frame 1 and frame 3 (the two comparable static poses) - they measured 101x99 vs 111x105 on the 128 canvas (~9% mismatch), so both were corrected toward their shared average via pivot-anchored rescale (frame 1 x1.040, frame 3 x0.963, both anchored at the fixed pivot (64,123)), landing at 106x104 vs 107x101 after correction. Frame 2 (the spin-blur) was deliberately left unmeasured/uncorrected: the row-profiling body-silhouette method is not meaningful for it (most of its pixels are the excluded cyan/white glow trail, not opaque body material), and its larger, more dynamic footprint is treated as an intentional effect (comparable to how Air Dash is expected to use stretch/afterimage per animation-policy.md section 8), not a jitter bug to fix. All 3 frames still share the same crop/scale and the same fixed pivot (64,123) as the other animations. loop is false (unlike Idle/Walking/Sprinting) since Turn is a one-shot transition, not a repeating cycle. 2026-09-10 (later same day): Jumping animation added (previous manifest backed up at proto_one.manifest.json.bak-before-jumping). Jumping=3 frames was adopted in animation-policy.md's Current Animation Contract (raw source had exactly 3 frames; code MovementState Jumping maps to this doc's Jump Start (~1) + Airborne (~1-2) combined, whose candidate ranges sum to ~3, so no conflict). All 3 raw frames are the same pose category (unlike Turn) - no mirrored or effect-only frame here, though frame 2 (jumping02) does carry a bright downward thrust-trail effect on its hover pods. Body-silhouette measurement (same blue-channel glow exclusion, re-verified against a debug mask) showed width very consistent across all 3 (90-94px on the 128 canvas, ~4%) but frame 2's body height measured shorter (86px vs 94px for the other two, ~8.5%). This was deliberately NOT corrected with a pivot-anchored rescale: visual inspection of the contact sheet shows the head/dome - the dominant silhouette element - is the same size in all 3 frames, and the height gap is concentrated in the hover-pod region only, consistent with pods being drawn tucked closer to the body during active thrust versus hanging relaxed at rest. A uniform rescale would incorrectly shrink the already-correct head to chase a pose difference, not a scale error, so no correction was applied - unlike Walking/Turn where the same tool WAS the right fix because the discrepancy there was a uniform whole-body scale inflation. fps=8/loop=false are independent candidates (Jumping is treated as a bounded one-shot takeoff, not a repeating cycle), not part of the Current Animation Contract. 2026-09-10 (later same day): Falling animation added (previous manifest backed up at proto_one.manifest.json.bak-before-falling). Falling=3 frames was adopted in animation-policy.md's Current Animation Contract (raw source had exactly 3 frames; code MovementState Falling maps to this doc's Airborne (~1-2), so the provided count exceeds that non-binding candidate range - documented as such rather than silently ignored). All 3 raw frames are the same pose category, no mirrored or effect-only frame. Body-silhouette measurement showed width tight across all 3 (95-96px on the 128 canvas) but frame 0 (falling01) measured notably shorter (95px height vs 102-104px for the other two, ~8% gap) while frames 1 and 2 already agreed closely with each other (102 vs 104, ~2%). This pattern - one frame off, the other two mutually consistent - matches the Walking-type uniform-scale-error case rather than the Jumping-type intentional-pose-difference case, so frame 0 alone was corrected via pivot-anchored rescale (x1.047 about the fixed pivot (64,123)), landing at 100x98px, in range with the other two. Falling is set to loop=true (unlike Turn/Jumping) since a fall's duration varies with height and isn't a fixed one-shot burst; fps=6 is an unconfirmed independent candidate. Not part of the Current Animation Contract, which governs frame count only. 2026-09-11: FastFalling animation added (previous manifest backed up at proto_one.manifest.json.bak-before-fastfalling). FastFalling=2 was adopted in animation-policy.md's Current Animation Contract (raw source had exactly 2 frames, matching the existing Fast Fall / Dive candidate range of ~1-2 exactly - no discrepancy to flag this time). Both raw frames render with a visible checkerboard pattern when previewed directly (fast_falling01 especially), which looked like the generator failing to produce real transparency. Verified this was NOT a real defect: pixel inspection showed alpha was already correct (0 in the background), and compositing the untouched raw file with true SourceOver alpha blending onto a solid test background produced a perfectly clean result with no checkerboard bleed - the checkerboard was a preview-only rendering quirk of the raw RGB values sitting under fully-transparent pixels, not a compositing defect. As a precaution against a separate real risk (bicubic interpolation sampling checkerboard-tinted RGB from adjacent transparent pixels into the resize, causing edge fringing), both raw frames were still sanitized before normalization: any pixel with 0<alpha<128 was snapped to fully transparent (RGB zeroed), and any pixel with 128<=alpha<255 was snapped to fully opaque, eliminating the genuinely semi-transparent edge-noise pixels (744 in fast_falling01, ~10000 in fast_falling02) that did carry checkerboard-contaminated RGB. Raw source files on disk were NOT modified; sanitized copies were used only as the input to the normalization pipeline. Both frames' full bbox was pixel-identical (X[271,967] Y[253,1072]) and body-silhouette bbox was very close (98x100 vs 98x102 on the 128 canvas, ~2%), so no per-frame outlier correction was needed. Both frames share the same crop/scale and the same fixed pivot (64,123) as every other animation. FastFalling is set to loop=true (like Falling, unlike Turn/Jumping) since dive duration is state-held, not a fixed burst; fps=10 is an unconfirmed independent candidate. 2026-09-11 (later same day): AirDashing animation added (previous manifest backed up at proto_one.manifest.json.bak-before-airdashing). AirDashing=3 was adopted in animation-policy.md's Current Animation Contract (raw source had exactly 3 frames, exceeding the non-binding Air Dash candidate range of ~2 - documented as such). All 3 raw frames are the same dash-pose category (unlike Turn, no mirrored/categorically-different frame), each carrying dash-stretch and cyan afterimage/speed-particle effects of varying intensity. Body-silhouette measurement (blue-channel glow/streak exclusion, re-verified with a debug mask) found air_dashing_02 (-> normalized frame 01) as a genuine uniform-scale outlier, not a pose difference: both width and height were proportionally smaller than the other two (102x91 vs 109x97 and 103x103 on the 128 canvas), unlike Jumping's case where only the pod region differed while the head stayed consistent. Corrected with a pivot-anchored rescale (x1.069 about the fixed pivot (64,123)) on that single frame only; the other two were left untouched. Post-fix the three frames read as consistently sized on the contact sheet. loop=false and fps=20 (much faster than any other animation) reflect that air dash is a short, fixed-duration burst (~0.14s per the movement prototype's dashDuration constant) re-triggered fresh each activation, not a held/looping state - closer in nature to Turn/Jumping than to Falling/FastFalling. 2026-09-11 (later same day): user expanded raw frames/fast_falling from 2 to 4 candidate frames (fast_falling03.png, 04.png added) and asked Claude to judge whether all 4 should be used. Measured: fast_falling01/02 have near-identical body aspect ratio (H/W 1.01 and 1.03, body ~696x701 and ~697x716) - the body silhouette itself stays round/compact, only streak-line intensity differs. fast_falling03/04 are a categorically different silhouette (H/W 1.21 and 1.15, body ~647x782 and ~656x757) - the stretch effect there reshapes the actual body silhouette into an elongated teardrop. First-pass decision was to keep 01+02 (backed up at proto_one.manifest.json.bak-before-fastfalling-4frame-review) - SUPERSEDED almost immediately by the next round below. 2026-09-11 (later same day, second round): user clarified the actual intent - FastFalling was always meant to be its own distinct 'more extreme dive' feel (not just Falling-but-faster), and 03/04 were generated specifically because 01/02 felt too weak in real gameplay; 03/04 are a *replacement* candidate set for 01/02, not a 4-frame extension of them. User tried chaining 01->04 and found it 'not bad' but ultimately asked Claude to choose among: (A) chain all 4, (B) use only 03+04, (C) keep 01+02, stating explicitly they want a stronger effect. Decision: (B), replacing 01+02 with 03+04. Reasoning: (C) directly contradicts the stated 'stronger effect' goal, ruling it out. Between (A) and (B): 03 and 04 measure much closer to each other in body aspect ratio (1.21 vs 1.15, ~5% apart) than 01/02 are to 03/04 (~20% apart), so a 03<->04 loop is far less likely to show a seam pop than a 01->02->03->04->01 loop would (which still snaps from the most-stretched frame back to the compact one every cycle) - and (A) also dilutes the intensity by presenting the weak silhouette half the time, working against the explicit goal. IMPORTANT technical difference from the first round: fast_falling03/04 were NOT run through the binary alpha-snap sanitizer used for 01/02 (and used in the FIRST attempt at evaluating 03/04's raw bbox) - pixel sampling showed their semi-transparent pixels (~370-387k px, vs 01/02's few-hundred/~10k edge-noise pixels) are a genuine smooth color-consistent alpha gradient (e.g. sampled RGBA(231,169,1,136) - the actual yellow body color fading out, not checkerboard-gray contamination spread across alpha 32-223 fairly evenly) representing the intended soft smear tail; binarizing it would have visibly blunted the smear effect the user explicitly wants more of, so the raw files were fed into the normalization crop/resize directly, unmodified. Crop was fit using a low alpha threshold (10, not the usual 200) specifically so the soft smear tail is not clipped out of the shared crop rectangle. Body-silhouette bbox on the final 128 canvas came out nearly identical (84x100 vs 84x98), so no per-frame outlier rescale was needed. fast_falling01.png and 02.png remain on disk, unused.
